intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls lining the park paths. A magical family-friendly cultural tradition that defines spring in Japan.
experiences.best_time_of_day: late afternoon into evening for illuminated blossoms

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market with the family, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha soft-serve, and grilled seafood skewers. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere, colorful stalls, and the chance to taste authentic Japanese street food culture firsthand.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will be thrilled feeding the monkeys while parents enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a visit to nearby Tenryu-ji Temple garden for a full cultural day.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art at teamLab Borderless in Azabudai Hills. Walk through rooms of flowing light, blooming digital cherry blossoms, and interactive installations that respond to your movement. A uniquely Japanese fusion of technology and art that captivates all ages and creates unforgettable memories.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a meaningful family journey to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Museum and Park to learn about history and resilience, then hop on a ferry to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Feed friendly deer roaming freely on the island, hike forested trails, and enjoy local Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki for lunch.
experiences.best_time_of_day: full day starting in the morning
experiences.location: Hiroshima city and Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Kansai/Itami Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for convenient transit use throughout the trip. Grab a quick convenience store meal from 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel — a great budget-friendly Japanese experience in itself.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Convenience store (konbini) meal: onigiri, bento box, or cup ramen — budget approx ¥500-¥800

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it simple. Focus on getting to the hotel safely. Convenience stores in Japan are exceptionally high quality and perfect for late-night arrivals. Rest well for the busy days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to enjoy the fresh morning air. Head to a nearby local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) for a budget morning set. Then explore the surrounding neighborhood on foot to get oriented — look for any local morning markets or shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby public park or waterfront area for a relaxed cherry blossom viewing session (hanami). April 16 should still be within cherry blossom season. Bring snacks from a convenience store and enjoy a casual picnic under the blossoms — a quintessential Japanese family activity at zero cost.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local shotengai (shopping arcade) near the resort for dinner. Look for a teishoku restaurant (set meal restaurant) offering rice, miso soup, and a main dish for ¥700-¥1,200. Browse 100-yen shops like Daiso for fun, affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten morning set (coffee + toast + egg) — approx ¥500-¥700
meals.lunch: Convenience store picnic under the cherry blossoms — approx ¥600-¥900
meals.dinner: Local teishoku restaurant set meal — approx ¥800-¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag recovery day — keep the pace relaxed. Let kids enjoy the open park space. Purchase any missing travel essentials at the 100-yen shop today.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kyoto! Take the JR train early to maximize time. Head straight to Maruyama Park for the famous Cherry Blossom Viewing (hanami) under Kyoto's iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura). Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Entry to the park is FREE. Walk through the adjacent Yasaka Shrine at no cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Gion district — Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Stroll Hanamikoji Street for free. Visit Kenninji Temple (¥500 adult, children free or discounted) — one of Kyoto's oldest Zen temples with beautiful gardens. Grab lunch at Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — try fresh tofu skewers, tamagoyaki, and pickles from market stalls for ¥100-¥300 each.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Kiyomizudera Temple area at dusk for stunning views over Kyoto (admission ¥400). Stroll the charming Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops. Return to hotel via JR train. Dinner at a gyudon chain (Yoshinoya or Sukiya) near the station.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market food stalls — approx ¥800-¥1,200
meals.dinner: Gyudon beef bowl chain restaurant — approx ¥500-¥700

day_by_day.notes: This is the Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park featured experience! Saturday will be busy — arrive at Maruyama Park as early as possible. Kids will love the festive hanami atmosphere with food stalls. Total transport cost: approx ¥1,500-¥2,000 round trip depending on hotel location.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arashiyama, Kyoto! Take the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama Station. Walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — completely FREE and magical for families. Children will love the towering bamboo tunnels. Visit Tenryuji Temple garden (¥500 adult, ¥300 child) with its classic Zen garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 adult, ¥250 child) — kids will absolutely love feeding and observing the Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Afterward, stroll along the Oi River and cross Togetsukyo Bridge for free scenic views. Browse the charming Arashiyama shopping street for affordable snacks and small souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Visit a local sento (public bathhouse) for a relaxing family soak — typically ¥400-¥500 per person, a genuine cultural experience. Dinner at a nearby ramen shop for a hearty, budget-friendly meal.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Arashiyama street food — matcha soft serve, warabi mochi, yudofu (tofu hot pot) — approx ¥700-¥1,000
meals.dinner: Local ramen shop — approx ¥700-¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: This covers the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park featured experience! The Monkey Park hike is about 20 minutes uphill — manageable for families but wear comfortable shoes. Bring water. The monkeys are wild — follow all posted safety instructions with children.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Nara on a day trip — just 45-60 minutes from Kyoto by train. Visit Nara Park (FREE entry) where over 1,000 friendly deer roam freely. Purchase shika senbei (deer crackers) for ¥200 to feed the deer — an unforgettable family activity. Walk to Todaiji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha (¥600 adult, ¥300 child).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner sanctum) with its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns. Walk the forested Kasugayama Primeval Forest path for free. Explore the Naramachi historic merchant district — free walking through preserved Edo-period townhouses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel area by early evening. Stop at a local izakaya (Japanese pub) near the resort for dinner — order shared small plates (yakitori, edamame, karaage) which are budget-friendly and great for families. Many izakayas have kid-friendly options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Nara kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) bento or local set lunch — approx ¥800-¥1,200
meals.dinner: Izakaya shared plates — approx ¥1,000-¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nara is extremely family-friendly. Young children may be startled by the bold deer — they will bow their heads if you bow to them! Keep food items hidden in bags as deer will try to eat anything. Round-trip train fare from Kyoto: approx ¥1,400.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka! Travel by JR or Hankyu train. Visit Osaka Castle (castle tower admission ¥600, grounds FREE) — beautiful with lingering cherry blossoms in the surrounding park. The castle tower has an excellent museum inside. Nishimaru Garden nearby is lovely for a short stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's famous entertainment district. Walk the canal area for free and marvel at the iconic Glico Running Man sign and giant mechanical crab. Visit the free Hozenji Yokocho alley. Take the kids to the interactive Cup Noodles Museum in nearby Ikeda (¥500 adult, free under 3) where you can create your own custom Cup Noodle (¥500 extra) — a beloved family activity.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Dotonbori — Osaka is Japan's food capital. Try takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500-¥600 for 8 pieces), okonomiyaki (savory pancake, ¥800-¥1,200), or kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers, ¥100-¥200 each). Return to hotel by 9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Osaka street food in Dotonbori — approx ¥700-¥1,000
meals.dinner: Dotonbori local restaurants — takoyaki, okonomiyaki — approx ¥800-¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is famous for 'kuidaore' (eating until you drop) — perfect for food-loving families on a budget. The street food scene is world-class and very affordable. Keep an eye on children in the busy Dotonbori crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at or near the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the beachfront for free family time. If there's a hotel pool or beach access, let the kids enjoy it. Take a leisurely walk along the coast and explore any nearby fishing villages or local morning markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local aquarium or family attraction (research specific options near the resort location). Alternatively, explore any remaining local cherry blossom spots — mid-April still offers beautiful blooms in many coastal areas. Visit a local shrine or small temple for a peaceful cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble a meal from a local supermarket (supermarkets in Japan have excellent ready-made sushi, bento, and hot foods at 20-30% discount after 7 PM). This is a great budget-saving strategy for families. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥700
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near resort — udon or soba set — approx ¥600-¥900
meals.dinner: Supermarket discounted bento/sushi — approx ¥500-¥800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day to recharge. Supermarket evening shopping is a brilliant budget hack in Japan — look for the yellow 'half price' stickers on bento and sushi after 7-8 PM. Great cultural experience for kids too!

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima. Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) — book in advance for best prices, or use a JR Pass if applicable. Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park (FREE entry to the park, ¥200 for the museum — deeply moving and educational for older children). See the iconic A-Bomb Dome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry ride (¥180 each way) to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's most scenic spots. See the famous floating Otorii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 entry). Walk the island and encounter freely roaming deer. Try Miyajima's famous momiji manju (maple leaf cakes, ¥150-¥200 each) — a must-eat local treat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city. Dinner at a local okonomiyaki restaurant — Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered with noodles) is a regional specialty at ¥800-¥1,200. Return to hotel by Shinkansen.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Miyajima Island — grilled oysters (local specialty, ¥300-¥500 each) and street food — approx ¥800-¥1,200
meals.dinner: Hiroshima okonomiyaki restaurant — approx ¥800-¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum contains graphic historical content — parental discretion advised for very young children. The museum is nonetheless important and educational. Miyajima is magical and very family-friendly with its friendly deer. Book Shinkansen tickets in advance for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Kyoto for a final cultural exploration. Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — the famous thousands of vermillion torii gates leading up the mountain. Entry is completely FREE and open 24 hours. Even a short 30-minute hike through the lower gates is spectacular and very family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a beautiful stone canal path lined with hundreds of cherry trees (still potentially blooming in late April). Walk from Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500) southward. Browse the artisan shops along the path for affordable crafts and pottery. Visit Nanzenji Temple (grounds FREE, sub-temples ¥400-¥600).
day_by_day.evening: Final Kyoto dinner at Pontocho Alley — a narrow atmospheric lane packed with restaurants at various price points. Look for restaurants with set dinner menus (teishoku) at ¥1,000-¥1,500. Stroll the illuminated alley after dinner for a magical final Kyoto evening. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx ¥400-¥600
meals.lunch: Obanzai (Kyoto-style small dishes) lunch set near Philosopher's Path — approx ¥900-¥1,300
meals.dinner: Pontocho Alley set dinner — approx ¥1,200-¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is best visited early morning or late afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The full hike to the summit takes 2-3 hours but even 30-45 minutes into the gates is rewarding. Wear comfortable shoes. Pontocho is atmospheric but choose restaurants carefully — look for posted menus with prices before entering.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure near Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last beachfront walk and take in the scenery. Visit any last local spots you missed. Do a final souvenir run at a nearby 100-yen shop or local omiyage (souvenir) shop for affordable gifts — Japanese Kit Kat flavors, local snacks, and small crafts make perfect budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (confirm checkout time). Head to the airport with ample time. Use your remaining IC card credit at the airport for last-minute shopping or snacks. Browse the airport's duty-free and souvenir shops — airport omiyage selections are excellent and competitively priced.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport — many airports have excellent ramen, sushi conveyor belt restaurants, and udon shops at reasonable prices. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Japan adventure!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — approx ¥500-¥800
meals.lunch: Light lunch near hotel or airport — convenience store or local shop — approx ¥500-¥700
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant — conveyor belt sushi or ramen — approx ¥800-¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ¥220 handling fee) — or keep it for a future Japan trip! Confirm flight check-in requirements and arrive at the airport at least 2.5-3 hours before international departure. Any unused yen can be exchanged at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport, clear customs and immigration, collect luggage. Take the Narita/Haneda Express or limousine bus to your hotel. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) near the hotel — try onigiri, hot noodles, or sandwiches. Budget-friendly and quintessentially Japanese.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30, so Day 1 is purely arrival and check-in. Rest well — you have a full 9 days ahead! Exchange some cash at the airport currency counter or use an ATM (7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards). Consider purchasing an IC card (Suica/Pasmo) for easy transit.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive early (around 8:00–9:00 AM) to experience the market at its liveliest. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats as a family. Wander the narrow stalls and soak up the vibrant atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum in Azabudai. Spend 2–3 hours immersed in the stunning interactive digital art installations — a magical, awe-inspiring experience for all ages. Book tickets in advance online to avoid sellouts.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the upscale Azabudai Hills complex surrounding teamLab. Enjoy dinner in the area before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi breakfast sets and tamagoyaki are iconic and affordable (¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)
meals.lunch: Continue snacking at Tsukiji or grab ramen at a nearby mid-range restaurant (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Azabudai Hills has a wide variety of restaurants — try Tonkatsu Maisen or a family-friendly Japanese izakaya for a sit-down meal (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited early morning. teamLab Borderless tickets should be pre-booked online (approximately ¥3,200 adults, ¥1,000 children). Wear comfortable shoes as teamLab involves a lot of walking and standing.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi/Hikari). Check in to your Kyoto accommodation or store luggage. Head straight to Maruyama Park for Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami). Admire Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in full bloom — mid-April is typically peak or late bloom season.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot. Visit Yasaka Shrine, walk the charming stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional shops and tea houses. Browse for souvenirs such as Kyoto ceramics and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Kyoto dinner in the Gion district. Keep an eye out for geiko (geisha) and maiko (apprentice geisha) as they make their evening rounds — Gion is most lively after dark.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick convenience store meal before boarding the Shinkansen
meals.lunch: Picnic-style hanami lunch in Maruyama Park — pick up bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or Nishiki Market (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa restaurant row — try Kyoto-style kaiseki set menu at a mid-range restaurant or enjoy yudofu (tofu hot pot), a Kyoto specialty (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Shinkansen tickets in advance or use a JR Pass if it offers value for your itinerary. Maruyama Park is free to enter. April 17 may still see beautiful cherry blossoms — check bloom forecasts closer to the date. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Higashiyama.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi to Arashiyama for the Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park experience. Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves early morning (before crowds arrive) for a serene, otherworldly atmosphere. Then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park to see Japanese macaques up close — kids absolutely love it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Arashiyama: visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), stroll along the Oi River, and cross the Togetsukyo Bridge. Rent a rowboat on the river for a fun family activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for an evening food walk — sample pickled vegetables, fresh mochi, skewered tofu, and local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kyoto hotel or a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Arashiyama has several mid-range restaurants along the main street — try soba noodles or a tofu cuisine set lunch (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market food walk for dinner — graze on various stalls (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 total per person) or sit down at a nearby izakaya

day_by_day.notes: Monkey Park admission is approximately ¥600 for adults, ¥300 for children. Tenryu-ji garden admission is ¥500. Arrive at the bamboo grove by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. The hike to Monkey Park takes about 20 minutes and involves uphill walking — manageable for families.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima: Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park. The museum offers a powerful, age-appropriate educational experience for families. Pay respects at the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Hiroshima's Ujina Port (or Miyajimaguchi) to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide — one of Japan's most photographed sights. Explore the shrine, meet the friendly wild deer roaming the island, and hike or take a ropeway up Mt. Misen for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry and Shinkansen to Kyoto. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departing for Hiroshima
meals.lunch: Hiroshima is famous for its okonomiyaki (savory pancakes with noodles) — eat at a local okonomiyaki restaurant near the Peace Park (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Casual Japanese restaurant near Kyoto hotel — try yakitori or a ramen shop for a comforting end to a meaningful day (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long but deeply rewarding day. Start early — aim to leave Kyoto by 8:00 AM. The Peace Memorial Museum is thoughtfully curated and suitable for children aged 8+; use parental discretion for younger kids. Check Miyajima tide schedules in advance for the best floating torii experience. Miyajima's famous momiji manju (maple-leaf cakes) make great snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Kyoto's iconic Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — walk through thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the forested mountain. The lower trail (30–45 minutes) is manageable for families; adventurous groups can hike higher. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp when walked upon — fascinating for kids and adults alike. Explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace and the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional tea ceremony experience in Kyoto. Several studios in the Higashiyama or Gion area offer family-friendly 45-minute sessions. Then take a peaceful evening walk along the Shirakawa Canal in Gion.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery/coffee shop near Fushimi Inari (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Street food stalls near Fushimi Inari offer inari sushi (rice in fried tofu pouches — the shrine's namesake food!) and grilled quail eggs (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in the Kawaramachi/Pontocho area — Pontocho Alley has excellent riverside restaurants with seasonal menus (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. Nijo Castle admission is approximately ¥1,000 per adult. Tea ceremony experiences range from ¥2,000–¥4,000 per person — book ahead online. Pontocho Alley is a narrow lantern-lit street with charming restaurants; reservations recommended for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Tokyo via Shinkansen (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes). Check in or drop luggage at Tokyo hotel. Head to the Asakusa district — visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional souvenirs, snacks, and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park nearby — in mid-to-late April, some cherry blossoms may still linger. Visit the Tokyo National Museum for a family-friendly introduction to Japanese history and art, or the Ueno Zoo (great for families with younger children). Ueno Park is also excellent for a relaxed afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) for an evening of neon lights, anime culture, video game arcades, and unique Japanese pop culture. Kids and teens especially love the multi-floor game centers.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kyoto hotel or grab an ekiben (station bento box) on the Shinkansen — a beloved Japanese travel tradition (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Asakusa area — try a tempura set lunch at Daikokuya (a historic tempura restaurant) or soba noodles at a local restaurant (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Akihabara has many mid-range options — try a themed café, a conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant, or a casual ramen shop (¥1,000–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji Temple is free and open daily. Tokyo National Museum admission is ¥1,000 for adults, free for children under 18. Ueno Zoo admission is ¥600 for adults, ¥200 for children. Akihabara is best experienced in the evening when the neon lights are brightest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's largest and most beautiful parks. Though peak cherry blossoms may be winding down, the garden is stunning in spring with late-blooming varieties and lush greenery. It's a perfect family picnic spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando. Walk down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and crepes — kids love the colorful scene. Then stroll the elegant Omotesando Boulevard for upscale shopping and architecture. Visit the Ota Memorial Museum of Art for ukiyo-e woodblock prints (optional, great for culture lovers).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing experience — watch the world's busiest pedestrian scramble from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation area. Explore Shibuya for dinner and evening entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery in Shinjuku (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen with convenience store bento boxes and drinks (¥800–¥1,500) — eating in the garden is a lovely experience
meals.dinner: Shibuya has excellent dining options — try Ichiran Ramen (solo ramen booths, a unique experience) or a family-friendly shabu-shabu restaurant (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen admission is ¥500 for adults, ¥250 for children. Note that alcohol is not permitted in the garden. Takeshita Street in Harajuku is pedestrian-only and very lively — best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Start with teamLab Planet (a separate immersive digital art experience from teamLab Borderless, focused on water and reflection art — equally stunning). Alternatively, explore the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and see the life-size Gundam statue outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy Odaiba's many family-friendly attractions: the Toyota Mega Web (car showcase, free), Palette Town Ferris Wheel for panoramic Tokyo Bay views, or the Odaiba Seaside Park with views of Rainbow Bridge and a replica Statue of Liberty. Kids can also enjoy the Joypolis indoor amusement park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo for a farewell dinner in the Ginza district — Tokyo's upscale shopping and dining hub. Splurge slightly on a special Japanese dinner to celebrate your trip. Afterward, enjoy a nighttime view of Tokyo from the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck in Shinjuku.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court at DiverCity or a mid-range restaurant on the waterfront — try Japanese curry or a burger (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ginza mid-range splurge — try a sushi restaurant with a set omakase menu or a teppanyaki restaurant for a memorable family experience (¥3,500–¥6,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked in advance online (approximately ¥3,200 adults, ¥1,000 children). Joypolis admission is approximately ¥800 entry + ride passes. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck is free and open until 11:00 PM on most nights — a fantastic free activity for the last evening.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Take a peaceful walk through the Imperial Palace East Gardens (free, open Tuesday–Sunday) in the heart of Tokyo. Admire the historic stone walls, moats, and spring flowers. Stop by the Kitanomaru Park nearby for a last look at Tokyo's greenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Nakamise in Asakusa or the basement food halls (depachika) of a major department store like Isetan in Shinjuku or Mitsukoshi in Ginza. Pick up Japanese snacks, wagashi (traditional sweets), and gifts to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport (Narita or Haneda) with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport — both Narita and Haneda have excellent restaurants and food options at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a proper sit-down meal before checking out (included or ¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Depachika food hall lunch — assemble a beautiful bento from the department store basement food halls (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant — both Narita and Haneda have great ramen, sushi, and tempura options airside (¥1,500–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in, security, and immigration at Narita. For Haneda, 2.5 hours is recommended. Use any remaining IC card balance at airport convenience stores or vending machines. Consider mailing excess luggage to the airport via takkyubin (luggage forwarding service) the day before to travel light on your last day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls lining the park paths. A magical family-friendly cultural tradition that defines spring in Japan.
experiences.best_time_of_day: late afternoon into evening for illuminated blossoms

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market with the family, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha soft-serve, and grilled seafood skewers. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere, colorful stalls, and the chance to taste authentic Japanese street food culture firsthand.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will be thrilled feeding the monkeys while parents enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a visit to nearby Tenryu-ji Temple garden for a full cultural day.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art at teamLab Borderless in Azabudai Hills. Walk through rooms of flowing light, blooming digital cherry blossoms, and interactive installations that respond to your movement. A uniquely Japanese fusion of technology and art that captivates all ages and creates unforgettable memories.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a meaningful family journey to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Museum and Park to learn about history and resilience, then hop on a ferry to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Feed friendly deer roaming freely on the island, hike forested trails, and enjoy local Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki for lunch.
experiences.best_time_of_day: full day starting in the morning
experiences.location: Hiroshima city and Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be arranged to whisk you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a late-night welcome amenity prepared by the resort — chilled sake, seasonal wagashi sweets, and a warm oshibori towel service. Check in and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated bento selection with miso soup, pickles, and green tea, available 24 hours

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer through the resort concierge before departure. Currency exchange or Suica card top-up can be handled at the airport arrival hall. Unpack minimally tonight — full exploration begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely premium breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Take a gentle walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Japan's time zone and breathe in the coastal air. Visit the resort's onsen spa for a revitalizing morning soak — a perfect introduction to Japanese bathing culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate coastal surroundings of the resort. Arrange a private guided cultural orientation tour through the concierge — a local expert will introduce you to nearby shrines, coastal fishing villages, and seasonal spring scenery. Stop at a local artisan shop to browse handcrafted ceramics and lacquerware as meaningful keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Kaiseki is Japan's most refined multi-course cuisine, featuring seasonal ingredients presented as edible art. Request a private tatami room for an authentic floor-seating experience with family.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort oceanfront restaurant — Japanese and Western buffet with fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, miso soup, seasonal fruit, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's beachside café — grilled fish teishoku set, cold soba noodles, and matcha latte
meals.dinner: Kaiseki multi-course dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — 10-course seasonal tasting menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day. Avoid heavy sightseeing to prevent exhaustion after the long-haul flight. Confirm upcoming day trip logistics with the concierge — particularly Kyoto and Tokyo transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle or Shinkansen to Kyoto. Upon arrival, head directly to Maruyama Park for the iconic Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Stroll beneath Kyoto's most celebrated weeping cherry tree, which is expected to be in glorious late bloom in mid-April. A private guide will share the cultural significance of hanami and the philosophy of 'mono no aware' — the bittersweet beauty of transience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After hanami, explore the adjacent Yasaka Shrine and the historic Gion district on foot. Browse traditional machiya townhouses, peek into artisan studios, and stop at a renowned wagashi confectionery to try handmade spring sweets. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — for a curated gourmet tasting walk with your guide, sampling tofu, pickles, and fresh yuba.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Gion. Many legendary establishments are tucked into restored machiya buildings along the canal. If fortunate, witness maiko or geiko (geisha apprentices) passing through the lantern-lit streets of Gion Hanamikoji on your evening stroll back.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure, or premium ekiben (station bento) purchased at Kyoto Station upon arrival
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market gourmet tasting walk — yuba tofu, Kyoto pickles, grilled skewers, and matcha soft serve
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred kaiseki at Kikunoi Honten or Nakamura in Gion — advance reservation essential, arrange through concierge

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April cherry blossoms in Kyoto may be in late bloom or petal-fall (hanafubuki) stage — both are breathtakingly beautiful. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Maruyama Park can be crowded; arriving before 9:00 AM offers a serene experience. Return to resort by private transfer in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Arashiyama district in western Kyoto (day trip from resort or continuing from Kyoto). Begin with a peaceful walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — towering green stalks create a cathedral-like canopy overhead. Arrive early to experience the grove before crowds gather. A private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the bamboo and surrounding gardens is a premium family highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bamboo grove, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park — a family favorite where Japanese macaques roam freely on the mountainside. The summit offers panoramic views over Kyoto. Descend and visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden, then browse the charming Arashiyama shopping street for bamboo crafts, matcha treats, and handmade paper goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private family onsen session (book a private rotenburo — outdoor bath) followed by an in-room premium dinner service. The resort can arrange a personal chef to prepare a teppanyaki dinner in your suite — wagyu beef, seasonal vegetables, and fresh seafood grilled tableside.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or early bento prepared by the resort for travel
meals.lunch: Arashiyama — Shigetsu vegetarian shojin ryori (Buddhist cuisine) at Tenryu-ji temple complex, or premium tofu kaiseki at Saga Tofuya Ukai
meals.dinner: In-suite private teppanyaki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — A5 Wagyu beef, lobster, and seasonal vegetables with sake and craft beer selection

day_by_day.notes: The Monkey Park hike involves a 20-minute uphill trail — suitable for families with children who enjoy light hiking. Bring water and wear sun protection. The rickshaw experience should be booked in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to Hiroshima and Miyajima Island. Depart early by Shinkansen (bullet train) — a premium Green Car experience is recommended for families. Arrive in Hiroshima and visit the Peace Memorial Museum and Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park. This deeply moving and historically significant experience is appropriate for older children and adults — a guided tour helps contextualize the history with sensitivity and hope.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the JR ferry to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's three most scenic views. The iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its floating torii gate is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. At high tide, the vermillion gate appears to float on the sea — a magical sight. Explore the island's stone-paved streets, interact with friendly wild deer, and climb partway up Mt. Misen via ropeway for sweeping island views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner on Miyajima Island before the return journey — Hiroshima oysters are a local specialty not to be missed. Return to the resort by Shinkansen and private transfer. Tonight is a quiet wind-down evening.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast or premium station bento on the Shinkansen — Green Car meal service available
meals.lunch: Hiroshima — okonomiyaki (savory pancake) at Micchan or a premium restaurant near Peace Park — Hiroshima-style with noodles is a must-try
meals.dinner: Miyajima Island — fresh Hiroshima oysters grilled, steamed, and fried at a waterfront restaurant; anago (conger eel) over rice is another island specialty

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum contains graphic historical content — review with children beforehand and allow emotional processing time. The floating torii gate visibility depends on tide schedules — check times in advance with your guide. This is a long but profoundly rewarding day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent morning. Book a premium spa treatment at the resort — a traditional Japanese shiatsu massage or hot stone therapy using locally sourced volcanic stones. Families can enjoy the resort pool or beachfront activities together.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a private cultural workshop arranged by the resort — options may include Japanese calligraphy (shodo), ikebana flower arranging with spring blooms, or a matcha tea ceremony conducted by a certified tea master in a traditional tatami room. These intimate experiences are ideal for families seeking hands-on cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace — sip yuzu sake cocktails, craft Japanese whisky highballs, and seasonal mocktails for younger family members as the sun dips below the horizon. Dinner at the resort's premium sushi counter — an omakase (chef's choice) experience where the head sushi chef prepares each piece individually before you.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — full Japanese set with grilled fish, rice, miso, and pickles alongside freshly squeezed citrus juice
meals.lunch: Resort beachside café — wagyu beef burger with truffle fries, fresh seafood salad, and cold craft beer or iced matcha
meals.dinner: Resort omakase sushi counter — 15-piece premium nigiri progression with seasonal toppings, miso soup, and dessert mochi

day_by_day.notes: This recovery day recharges the family for the upcoming Tokyo days. Confirm all Tokyo bookings — teamLab Borderless tickets, Tsukiji tour, and restaurant reservations — through the concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Tokyo. Depart by Shinkansen (Green Car) or domestic flight — arrange private transfer to the station or airport. Upon arriving in Tokyo, check into a luxury day-use lounge or the resort's Tokyo partner hotel to freshen up. Begin exploration in the Shibuya and Harajuku districts — witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, browse Omotesando's luxury boutiques, and explore Takeshita Street's quirky youth fashion scene with the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum in Azabudai Hills — an unmissable, world-renowned immersive digital art experience. Entire families are enchanted by the boundaryless rooms where art flows across floors, walls, and ceilings. Interactive installations respond to touch and movement — children and adults alike lose themselves in wonder for hours. Pre-book timed entry tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the upscale Azabudai Hills or Roppongi area — dine at a premium Japanese restaurant with city views. Alternatively, visit a rooftop bar for Tokyo skyline cocktails before a refined dinner. Return to accommodation by private car.

meals.breakfast: On Shinkansen — premium bento from Kyoto Station or resort-prepared travel lunch box
meals.lunch: Omotesando — lunch at a chic Japanese bistro or the iconic Omotesando Hills food hall; try wagyu beef sandwiches or premium ramen at a top-rated establishment
meals.dinner: Azabudai Hills — premium kaiseki or contemporary Japanese cuisine at a Michelin-recognized restaurant; Florilège or Sazenka are exceptional choices

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before the trip or have the concierge secure tickets. The museum is best enjoyed with 2–3 hours allocated. Wear comfortable shoes and be prepared to remove them in some installations.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Tokyo's legendary culinary playground. A private guide leads the family through bustling market lanes, introducing vendors who have supplied Tokyo's finest restaurants for generations. Sample fresh uni (sea urchin), premium otoro tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled egg), fresh oysters, and crispy tempura. This is a world-class foodie experience that delights all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Asakusa — Tokyo's most historic district. Visit the magnificent Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, and stroll the Nakamise shopping street for traditional souvenirs: folding fans, kokeshi dolls, ningyo-yaki cakes, and handmade chopsticks. A private rickshaw tour of Asakusa's historic backstreets offers a premium and comfortable way to see the area. Cross the Sumida River for views of Tokyo Skytree.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend Tokyo Skytree to the Tembo Deck (350m) or Tembo Galleria (450m) for breathtaking panoramic night views of the city — on clear evenings, Mt. Fuji is visible on the horizon. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Skytree complex or nearby Sumida area. Alternatively, dine at a renowned tempura or sukiyaki restaurant in Ginza for a classic Tokyo fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour — breakfast IS the tour; fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, clam soup, and seasonal tastings
meals.lunch: Asakusa — premium unaju (eel over rice) at Asakusa Mugitoro or Daikokuya, a historic eel restaurant beloved since 1887
meals.dinner: Ginza — Sukiyaki at Ginza Shabu-zen or premium tempura omakase at Kondo or Mikawa Zezankyo — reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant between 6:00–10:00 AM. Arrive early for the best selection and fewest crowds. The market is cash-friendly — carry yen. Asakusa can be busy on weekends; the rickshaw experience helps navigate comfortably with family.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Imperial Palace East Gardens — a serene, beautifully maintained public garden surrounding the Imperial Palace in central Tokyo. Cherry blossom trees may still offer late blooms or fresh green foliage in mid-April. A private guided walk contextualizes the Edo-era history of the palace grounds. Nearby, visit the Kitanomaru Park and Nippon Budokan area for additional scenic strolling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island — for family-friendly exploration. Visit the teamLab Planets art installation (a separate, equally stunning experience from Borderless), the life-size Gundam statue, and the Miraikan science museum. Enjoy the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the replica Statue of Liberty. Odaiba's DiverCity and Venus Fort offer premium shopping and dining.
day_by_day.evening: Final Tokyo evening — celebrate with a premium wagyu beef dinner. Book a private dining room at a renowned wagyu steakhouse for a tableside A5 Kuroge Wagyu experience — the pinnacle of Japanese beef culture. Toast the journey with Japanese whisky from a curated selection. Return to accommodation and begin light packing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or accommodation breakfast — Japanese set with grilled salmon, rice, miso, and pickles
meals.lunch: Odaiba — premium ramen at Fuunji (if visiting Shinjuku en route) or a seafood lunch at a waterfront Odaiba restaurant with Rainbow Bridge views
meals.dinner: Celebration wagyu dinner — Aragawa, Beefsteak Kawamura, or Yoroniku in Tokyo — A5 Wagyu tasting with Japanese whisky pairing; reserve the private room

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets in Toyosu (near Odaiba) requires separate tickets from Borderless — book in advance. The wagyu dinner is the trip's culinary centerpiece — confirm the reservation 48 hours before. Pack souvenirs and gifts tonight to avoid morning rush.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a premium hotel breakfast without rushing. Take a quiet walk through a nearby garden or park — Shinjuku Gyoen or Yoyogi Park offer a peaceful farewell to Japan's spring beauty. Last-minute luxury shopping at Isetan Shinjuku or Mitsukoshi Ginza — pick up premium Japanese tea, whisky, cosmetics, and confectionery as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport — allow 2–3 hours before departure. At the airport, visit the premium terminal lounges (ANA Suite Lounge or JAL First Class Lounge) for a refined pre-flight experience with Japanese cuisine, craft sake, and serene interiors. Browse duty-free for last-minute Japanese whisky, cosmetics, and wagashi sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Board departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's most iconic experiences — cherry blossoms, ancient temples, cutting-edge art, world-class cuisine, and the warmth of omotenashi (Japanese hospitality) at every turn.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — full Japanese set or Western option; savor every last bite of Japanese cuisine
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge — curated Japanese lunch with soba, sushi, and seasonal dishes; or a farewell ramen at a renowned airport ramen restaurant
meals.dinner: On board flight — request premium meal in advance; or enjoy the airline's business/first class Japanese cuisine service

day_by_day.notes: Depart the hotel no later than 3–4 hours before your flight to account for Tokyo traffic and airport check-in. Ensure all duty-free liquids (whisky, sake) are packed in checked luggage or purchased after security. Keep omiyage (souvenir gifts) accessible for customs declaration if required. Carry a copy of all accommodation and activity receipts for potential customs inquiries.
